# prism-uorc Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism UORC: Decides whether one object may be kept in, or opened from, the owner's browser as a UORC archive (UOR-Foundation/compression): the archive is the object's reference, a lossless executable structure sealed by UORC-SHA256-CHAIN-v1, named by the kappa label of the bytes it restores. The decision reads only the archive's structure (its seal, format, scope, object count, whether it restored to the very bytes its label names, and the kappa facet's answer), never the content: values are projected only when the decision says open.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because the kill switch stops every keep and open.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `keep yes ok known self one same admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always refuse when seal is broken

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when seal is broken, because an archive whose seal does not check is no reference.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `open no broken known self one same admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Always refuse when format is other

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when format is other, because only the pinned client's format and profile are read.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `keep no ok other self one same admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Always refuse when scope is other

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when scope is other, because an archive conditional on a basis the browser does not hold cannot be checked here.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `keep no ok known other one same admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Always refuse when objects is many

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when objects is many, because one archive is one object under one kappa label.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `keep no ok known self many same admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Always refuse when restore is differs

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when restore is differs, because an archive that restores other bytes than its label names is never kept or opened.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `open no ok known self one differs admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: Always refuse when restore is failed

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when restore is failed, because an archive that does not decode within the work bound is never kept or opened.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-007, theorem `inv007Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-007 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `open no ok known self one failed admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: Always refuse when kappa is other

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when kappa is other, because an object the kappa facet did not admit has no reference in the Prism.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-008, theorem `inv008Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-008 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `keep no ok known self one same other` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: Never open when act is keep

The app SHALL NOT answer `open` when act is keep, because keeping never projects the object's values.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-009, theorem `inv009Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-009 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `keep no ok known standard one same admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `open`
- **AND** the app answers `keep`, decided by REQ-009

### Requirement: Never keep when act is open

The app SHALL NOT answer `keep` when act is open, because opening never writes.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-010, theorem `inv010Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-010 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `open no ok known standard one same admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `keep`
- **AND** the app answers `open`, decided by the fallback

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `keep yes ok known self one same admit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-001, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 8 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `keep`, `open`, `refuse`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `act` | `keep`, `open` | keep: the vault is about to keep the object as this archive; open: the vault is about to give the object back from this archive |
| `halted` | `no`, `yes` | the kill switch |
| `seal` | `ok`, `broken` | the archive's UORC-SHA256-CHAIN-v1 integrity seal checks (inspect's integrity_ok), read without decoding |
| `format` | `known`, `other` | the archive's format and machine profile are the ones the pinned client writes (format 2, profile 1) |
| `scope` | `self`, `standard`, `other` | self-contained; conditional on the standard basis the pinned client carries (named by its identity in site/uorc/uorc.lock.json); or conditional on any other basis, which the browser does not hold |
| `objects` | `one`, `many` | the archive restores exactly one object, the one its kappa label names |
| `restore` | `same`, `differs`, `failed` | the archive decoded within the client's work bound to the very bytes its kappa label names (same), to other bytes, or not at all |
| `kappa` | `admit`, `other` | the kappa facet's answer for the restored bytes under their label: admit, or anything else |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `keep` | the archive is kept as the object's reference |
| `open` | the archive's values are projected for the owner |
| `refuse` | the archive is neither kept nor opened |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 8 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `keep no ok known standard one same admit` gives `keep`
- `open no ok known standard one same admit` gives `open`
- `keep no ok known self one same admit` gives `keep`
- `keep yes ok known self one same admit` gives `refuse`
- `open no broken known self one same admit` gives `refuse`
- `keep no ok other self one same admit` gives `refuse`
- `keep no ok known other one same admit` gives `refuse`
- `keep no ok known self many same admit` gives `refuse`
- `open no ok known self one differs admit` gives `refuse`
- `open no ok known self one failed admit` gives `refuse`
- `keep no ok known self one same other` gives `refuse`
- `keep no ok known self one same` gives `invalid`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
